_doc: Crew defaults and job numbers (read by scripts/crew/crew_member.gd config(), jobs.gd, and fire.gd for room names). hp: the health of a crew member whose species data/species.json does not list (each species sets its own). damage_per_s: fire (standing in a burning cell) and no_air (room pressure below no_air_below, a fraction). heal_per_s: lying on a bed or in a powered medbay (the medbay's stats.heal multiplies it); neither heals anybody who breathes while its room is under no_air_below. revive_hp: health a downed crew member comes back with. bleed_out_s: seconds a downed crew member (not the player's soldier) lies at 0 hp before they die (scripts/crew/mortality.gd); the timer stops while a crewmate works a revive on them or they lie in a room with a powered, working medbay. ion_hp: hit points an ion hit costs each crew member in the room it lands in, per point of its damage (times their damage_taken.ion; see Jobs.ion_hit, which also applies ion_stun). player and ada: the two people every ship starts with (name and PersonDrawer palette). extra_crew: more NPCs spawned at beds, named from names in order and coloured from looks in order. enemy: the crew of a ship that is not the player's (count, names, one palette). jobs: period is how often the job board is rebuilt and handed out (seconds); switch_margin is how much higher a new job's priority must be to pull a crew member off the one they are doing; search limits the work of picking (jobs: how many of the nearest jobs get a path, spots: how many standing spots per job, paths: path searches per hand-out); order_hold is how long a crew member ignores the board after a manual order (middle click). Per job: priority, seconds (work time, times the line's repair multiplier), rate (extinguish: intensity removed per crew member per second; repair_crew: hit points a second restored to a hurt `mechanical` crew member, who beds do not heal), slots (crew that may work it at once). repair_component adds combat_bonus to the priority of parts of combat_families while a fight is on. man_station applies to helm and to the families listed when the part has manned: true; out of a fight the other stations lose idle_penalty from their priority, so the helm is manned first (the autopilot in sector space needs it). restock (priority 40, rate = units carried a second, slots) carries ammo from the cargo to an ammo rack below half full (scripts/sim/ammo.gd; the work_mult restock of the crew scales it); repair_belt (priority, seconds, slots) mends one conveyor-belt cell that damage cut. repair_block (priority, calm_bonus, seconds_per_hp, slots) mends a wall or door tile that is below its hp and not breached (a breach is repair_breach): the priority is 60 in a fight and 60 + calm_bonus out of one, below every other repair, and the work is seconds_per_hp for each hp missing times the tile line's repair multiplier; it is done by the crew, the drones and the soldier's hand (E). clear_wreck (priority, seconds, slots) clears the debris of a part that was wrecked (docs/CONTENT.md 4f) and gives back half its recipe materials, rounded down. drone: the repair drone (playtest 2, R1; species `drone` in data/species.json): species is its species id, item the cargo item that turns into one (data/items.json, recipes.json), name the first drone's name (the next ones are Name 2, Name 3 ...), power what each working drone draws from the ship's surplus with no cable (Power.feed_drones; a drone with no power stands still). drone_jobs: the only jobs a drone is handed (Jobs._pick): never a station, a revive, a crewmate's mending or an order; a broken drone (0 hp) gets the repair_crew job like any mechanical crew member. manned: helm_evasion is the evasion a manned helm adds in combat (the arena may read ship.manned later); weapon_cooldown is the fraction a manned weapon's cooldown is shortened by; process_speed is the fraction a manned smelter works faster by (docs/CONTENT.md section 12: 0.3; scripts/craft/processing.gd; a smelter is only manned while it has a queue). room_names: the first family found in a room names it in the chronicle. labels: the words of the HUD crew line ({name} is the part, {who} the crew member). traits: crew member name -> list of personal trait ids (ids of the trait library, data/traits.json: suit wears an EVA suit, no_breath, heat_resistant ...); a name that is not listed has none. CrewMember.traits() merges them with the species' traits (data/species.json) and worn gear, and TraitSet.of() (scripts/crew/traits.gd) turns the merged traits into numbers; abilities.gd checks the merged list against an ability's operator_needs. posts (playtest 2, K1): families lists the part families that can be posted besides the helm and every part with manned: true (the station bar shows one button for each; Posts.stations); a crew member posted to a part mans it for good (CrewMember.post) and leaves only for a fire in its room, a breach in its room, repairing the part itself or restocking the ammo rack that feeds the gun (Posts.allows). air (K3): a breathing crew member (not a drone, not vacuum_walk or o2_use 0, not wearing a suit) whose hp falls under hurt_below (a fraction of max hp) walks out of a room with pressure under no_air_below and takes no jobs in such a room until their hp is over back_above; breath_ok is the pressure a room needs for them to walk into it (Evacuate.path_out). breach (K2): a room that falls under pressure (a fraction) because of a breach, with crew in it or on the way, raises a prompt (BreachAlert); slow_down false turns the slow-down off, time_scale is the speed while the prompt is up, prompt_s the real seconds to answer it (no answer is Repair) and gap_s the real seconds between two slow-downs (a second prompt waits for the first without slowing again); Evacuate abandons the room and walks everyone out to a room with pressure of at least breath_ok. breath_margin (repairs track): a crew member who breathes and wears no suit takes a job with a finite work time (a breach, a part, a wall, a belt, a wreck, a revive) in an airless room, or one whose walk crosses one, only when the seconds they have until air.hurt_below (from their hp now, at the room's suffocation rate: damage_per_s.no_air x their damage_taken.no_air x suffocate_mult) are at least breath_margin times the seconds spent in bad air: the walk in, the work still to do (at their work rate) and the walk out to air; one on such a job who can no longer finish it (the same sum, margin 1, plus the hand-out period) leaves before hurt_below, and the job stays on the board for the next. A breath_margin of 0 turns the budget off. The player's own orders are not held to it (Jobs.order_warning says so). lost (repairs track): in a fight a room is lost when the cells of its boundary (the walls and doors round it, shot-open ones included) that are shot open number at least max(min_open, share of the boundary cells); a lost room posts no jobs (like an abandoned room), the crew in it walk out to air and the ship records it in `lost_rooms` until the fight is over; the soldier's hand and the player's orders still work there. under_fire: a wall or part hit in the last `seconds` is repaired at `mult` of the speed (Damage.apply stamps ship.hit_at). slow (repairs track): the game speed while the fight slow-down (Tab, slow_down.gd) is on; the breach prompt's own time_scale is merged with it (time_scale.gd: the slower wins).
